title: VaR Mapping

maps.tested: The differentiation among the three mapping methods is the tested object, not the heavy derivative mapping. One sheet is explicit: 'do NOT worry about non-linear and linear derivatives: huge calculations may not show up.'
maps.specifics: Reported twice in identical wording: 'difference in VaR mapping: principal, duration, cash flow.' The sheet additionally singles out LO 5.f, 'especially interpretation of variance improvement': VaR relative to a performance benchmark. Principal mapping uses only the timing of principal; duration mapping uses portfolio duration; cash-flow mapping decomposes every payment onto the grid. Ranking their risk-capture fidelity is the classic comparison.

vardeezReading: MR-5: Important; differentiate principal, duration and cash-flow mapping, calculate principal and duration mapping, and above all interpret variance improvement (LO 5.f), but do not worry about linear and non-linear derivative mapping because huge calculations may not show up.

selectors.name: Principal, duration and cash-flow mapping differences
selectors.what: What distinguishes the three fixed-income mapping methods: principal mapping uses one risk factor at the average maturity of principal (redemption timing only), duration mapping uses one risk factor at the portfolio duration, cash-flow mapping places the present value of every payment on the vertices of the grid.

selectors.name: Benchmark VaR: tracking error, variance improvement
selectors.what: TE-VaR = alpha x sqrt((x - x0)' Sigma (x - x0)) for a portfolio against its benchmark, and the variance improvement 1 - (TE-VaR / VaR of the benchmark)^2, interpreted like an R-squared as the share of benchmark variance explained (about 95.4% in the book example: index VaR 1.99, TE-VaR 0.43).
selectors.theory: Why the ratio is squared (variance, not VaR, improvement; 1 - TE-VaR/VaR understates it), what the remaining tracking error means (nonparallel moves in the term structure), and why minimising absolute VaR is not minimising relative VaR (a barbell has the lowest absolute VaR but the worst tracking error).

selectors.name: Ranking the three methods by risk fidelity
selectors.what: Order the methods by how faithfully they capture market risk: cash-flow mapping best, then duration mapping, principal mapping crudest; principal mapping ignores intervening coupons and so gives the highest VaR of the three, while all three preserve market value.

selectors.name: Calculate principal and duration mapping VaR
selectors.source: Vardeez: 'Calculation of principal and duration mapping'; reading note 'calc of Principal & Duration mapping'
selectors.what: Principal mapping VaR = W x VaR rate at the average maturity; duration mapping VaR = W x VaR rate at the portfolio duration, with the rate linearly interpolated between the two neighbouring vertices: VD = Vj + (Vj+1 - Vj)(D - j). Book check: principal 2.97, duration 2.70, cash flow 2.63 undiversified and 2.57 diversified.
selectors.theory: Why the principal figure overstates risk, why duration sits between principal and cash flow, and the split of the gap between duration and diversified cash-flow VaR into non-linearity in maturity (2.70 to 2.63) and correlations below one (2.63 to 2.57).
